That makes Dupont only $23.19 more overall, subject to confirming how the Penn fee is taxed.

That is much closer than the nightly prices made it look. The Penn listing says maximum occupancy four, and it let me enter two adults and one child age 14. Dupont says the same, but its room description calls the balcony room suitable for up to four guests.

Then both appear valid for three guests on paper. Penn provides two double beds; Dupont provides two queens, and the exact Dupont listing also identifies a balcony. Before payment, the final booking screen should still name all three guests or show occupancy for three, retain the selected bed type, and display every mandatory charge.

Yes. For a family trip where we will actually have downtime at the hotel, I would prioritize the room with a balcony when it is available. It is not an absolute requirement, but here the price gap is small enough to matter.

That gives Dupont a meaningful room advantage: larger beds and the balcony for about $5.80 more per night after tax. Penn still has the stronger sightseeing location. Put numbers around Monday morning. Our Capitol tour check-in is 8:20 a.m., and I do not want the location comparison left vague.

Most of Saturday and Sunday will be Mall museums, but Friday evening and Tuesday morning are open. Does Dupont create enough inconvenience that Penn should still win?

That saves $285 against Southwest through DCA, but I do not think a 10:05 arrival at BWI is sensible with a teenager and luggage.

That is the main tradeoff. The BWI savings are meaningful, but the likely hotel arrival is around 11:20 p.m. or later, versus roughly 10:10 p.m. from DCA. It also takes more time from Tuesday and introduces a less predictable airport transfer.
Before choosing, how much museum time does the 5:30 DCA return really leave? Assume we check two bags.

We can check out, leave the bags with the hotel, visit the museum, and collect them around 2:45. That still gives us enough time.

How does seating work on that Southwest fare? For my own seat, request a window whenever selection is available.

Understood. Are both DAL and DFW workable? Also, will you check a bag, and how much arrival margin do you want before the 1:00 p.m. opening session?
Both airports are possible. Carry-on only. I am trying to decide whether flying Thursday morning is sensible at all. I would want to be at the meeting location by 11:30 if possible.

Thursday morning can work, but I would rule out flights landing after about 10:00 a.m. A 10:25 arrival may look acceptable on paper, yet deplaning and the drive from MCI could put you in the Crossroads around 11:30 or later with almost no recovery time. The Holiday Inn sounds more appropriate. Is it close enough, or would I be paying for rides back and forth to the meetings too?

The meetings are near 19th and Main. Use that. Show me complete combinations, including the Dallas rides.

So the American option is cheapest even though DFW transportation costs more. How dependable is that 8:55 arrival for being at 19th and Main by 11:30?

It gives a reasonable planning margin. Could I go directly to the hotel first, or does that create unnecessary risk?

Then give me the complete trip total for each one using the flight and ride estimates from the last comparison. Keep the $12 local transportation cushion in both.

Using the $267 American airfare, $103 for the two airport rides, and the $12 local transportation cushion: Holiday Inn Express totals $640.20 ($267 + $258.20 + $103 + $12). Choose the Holiday Inn Express at the working total of $258.20 for the night and $640.20 for the full trip. American moved my Friday Kansas City return up by seventy minutes. It now leaves at 6:25 p.m., and my meeting near 19th and Main still ends at 4:00. Is that workable?

It is possible only if the meeting ends on time and everything goes smoothly. Does a seventy-minute airline change let me switch for free, or would I owe the fare difference?

American's eligibility depends on the schedule-change terms attached to the ticket, but a departure moved by more than an hour commonly qualifies for a complimentary adjustment. Confirm that the reservation is flagged for a schedule change and that the 7:35 flight is offered as an eligible same-day alternative. If it is, there should be no change fee or fare difference.
Would you choose 7:35 over 9:10? I cannot leave the meeting early.

Yes. The 7:35 flight is the better balance. It gives enough time after a firm 4:00 finish to collect luggage and reach MCI without the tight margin of 6:25, while avoiding the much later arrival attached to 9:10.

Request a schedule-change reissue of only the Friday MCI-DFW segment to the 7:35 p.m. nonstop, preserving Thursday's DFW-MCI flight and the existing fare cabin. We settled on New Orleans for three nights and we are driving. Compare Saturday, December 20 through Tuesday, December 23 with Saturday, December 27 through Tuesday, December 30. It will be me, my spouse, and our 14-year-old in one room. I want to understand the French Quarter versus the Warehouse District versus somewhere just outside the busiest part, including parking.

I’ll compare one representative hotel in each area for both windows, using a room that explicitly permits three guests. Before I calculate totals, are you comfortable with either two queen beds or a king plus a sleeper sofa? Also, will the car remain parked for all three nights?

Two queens is much better. Assume we park it when we arrive and do not move it until checkout. Our main plans are the French Quarter, the World War II Museum, one evening meal around Magazine Street, and probably a riverfront walk.

That gives me a clean comparison. I found representative two-queen options at Hotel Monteleone in the French Quarter, Cambria Hotel New Orleans Downtown in the Warehouse District, and Hampton Inn & Suites New Orleans Downtown on Carondelet, which is in the central business district just outside the most crowded visitor blocks. Each room’s listed maximum occupancy is four, so two adults and one 14-year-old fit without a second room or rollaway.
Good. Show me the first date window with every lodging and parking charge separated. Do not treat parking as incidental.

For December 20-23, the Hotel Monteleone two-queen flexible rate is $289 per night: $867 room subtotal, $144.79 estimated hotel tax, and $1,011.79 lodging total. The Cambria two-queen rate is $219 per night: $657 room subtotal, $109.72 estimated hotel tax, and $766.72 lodging total. Valet is $48 per night, or $144, for a working total of $910.72 before parking tax. The Hampton two-queen rate is $199 per night: $597 room subtotal, $99.70 estimated hotel tax, and $696.70 lodging total. Valet is $45 per night, or $135, for a working total of $831.70 before parking tax.
You called those combined totals, but they still exclude tax on parking. Keep them as working estimates and flag that clearly. Now give me the later window on the same basis.

Correct. Those are lodging totals plus base valet charges, not final checkout totals, because the parking-tax line was not exposed consistently. For December 27-30, Hotel Monteleone is $339 per night: $1,017 room subtotal, $169.84 estimated hotel tax, $1,186.84 lodging total, and $177 base valet, producing a $1,363.84 working estimate before parking tax. Cambria is $249 per night: $747 room subtotal, $124.75 estimated hotel tax, $871.75 lodging total, and $144 base valet, producing a $1,015.75 working estimate before parking tax. Hampton is $229 per night: $687 room subtotal, $114.73 estimated hotel tax, $801.73 lodging total, and $135 base valet, producing a $936.73 working estimate before parking tax.
How much more is the later weekend for each one?

On the same working basis, the later window adds $175.05 at Hotel Monteleone, $105.03 at Cambria, and $105.03 at Hampton. Parking is unchanged in these estimates, so each difference comes from the room rate and associated lodging tax.
Now explain the locations in practical terms. We do not need to be on Bourbon Street, but I also do not want every outing to start with a car.

Hotel Monteleone gives the easiest French Quarter access: Royal Street is outside, Jackson Square is roughly a 10-minute walk, and the riverfront is about 10-15 minutes. The World War II Museum is the weak point at roughly 25-30 minutes on foot, so a streetcar or short rideshare may be preferable. Cambria reverses that balance: the museum is about a 5-8 minute walk, the Quarter edge about 15 minutes, Jackson Square closer to 20-25 minutes, and the riverfront around 15-20 minutes. Hampton on Carondelet is the middle position: about 8-12 minutes to the Quarter edge, 15-20 minutes to the riverfront, and 18-22 minutes to the museum. For a Magazine Street dinner, all three are reasonably served by a rideshare; Cambria starts slightly closer to the Lower Garden District.
What about noise and actually getting the car back Tuesday morning? I know you cannot guarantee a quiet room.

Hotel Monteleone is in the most active area, so street-facing rooms have the greatest potential for nighttime noise; an interior or higher-floor room would reduce risk but must be requested, not assumed. Cambria’s immediate blocks are less nightlife-heavy, though event and traffic noise can still occur. Hampton is outside the densest Quarter activity, but Carondelet is a transit and traffic corridor. All three are valet-only in these quotes. For Tuesday checkout, the practical issue is retrieval time: request the vehicle 20-30 minutes before departure, and allow longer at Hotel Monteleone if the lobby and curb are busy.
Verify the cancellation differences. Holiday wording is exactly where I do not want a vague answer.

The displayed December 20 rates were flexible, but the deadlines differed: Hotel Monteleone showed cancellation without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local time three days before arrival; Cambria showed 48 hours before arrival; Hampton showed 48 hours before arrival. For December 27, Hotel Monteleone displayed a seven-day cancellation deadline, Cambria displayed a seven-day deadline on the quoted rate, and Hampton displayed a 72-hour deadline. After those deadlines, the quoted terms indicated a one-night room-and-tax penalty. These terms are rate-specific, so the final booking screen must repeat the deadline in calendar-date form before payment.
And the room setup really accepts three people? I do not want a search result that quietly priced only two adults.

Yes. The comparison was run for two adults and one child age 14, and each quoted category was a two-queen room with a listed capacity of four. The price did not show an added third-person charge. Still verify that the checkout page carries all three guests forward, because some hotel sites reset occupancy when moving from search results to payment.
Take the Quarter hotel out unless there is a strong reason to pay that much. Compare Cambria and Hampton more closely for the first window.

For December 20-23, Hampton is $79.02 less on the working estimate: $831.70 versus Cambria’s $910.72, with both still excluding any tax assessed on valet. Hampton is the better value and slightly quicker for walking into the Quarter. Cambria is materially better for the World War II Museum, has a calmer transition to the Warehouse District restaurants, and is somewhat better positioned for a Magazine Street rideshare. Neither requires using the car for the Quarter, museum, or riverfront plans, though the museum walk from Hampton is longer.
Does breakfast change the comparison? Include only what is actually part of the rate.

Hampton’s quoted rate includes its standard hot breakfast for all three registered guests. Cambria’s quoted rate does not include breakfast. Even without assigning a dollar value, that widens Hampton’s cost advantage. Hotel Monteleone’s rate also did not include breakfast, but it is already out of the active comparison.
Which plan is strongest overall? I care about location enough to pay some difference, but I do not see a reason to spend more just to say we stayed in the Quarter.

The strongest overall plan is the December 20-23 stay at Cambria. It costs $79.02 more than Hampton on the current working basis, but it puts the World War II Museum within a very short walk, keeps the French Quarter and riverfront reachable without moving the car, and offers the better starting point for the Magazine Street evening. The earlier dates also save $105.03 compared with the same Cambria room December 27-30. Hampton is the value fallback if included breakfast and the lowest total matter more than shortening the museum walk.
Give me the exact verification list for Cambria, and do not reserve anything.

Before reserving Cambria for December 20-23, verify that the checkout page lists two adults and one 14-year-old in one two-queen room with a maximum occupancy of at least three; the room charges total $657; lodging tax is $109.72; and no destination, resort, or mandatory property fee appears. Confirm valet is $48 for each of three nights, ask for the parking-tax amount and any oversized-vehicle surcharge, and obtain a true lodging-plus-parking final total. And valet access? We should not need the car once it is parked, but I need to know whether Tuesday morning could become a problem.

Cambria’s valet is available around the clock, includes in-and-out access, and advises allowing about 20 to 30 minutes for retrieval during busy periods. Map the Saturday drive. I want actual stops and enough buffer for traffic coming into New Orleans.

Leave Dallas at 6:45 a.m. Take I-20 east toward Shreveport, then I-49 south through Alexandria and Lafayette before joining I-10 east. Stop near Longview around 8:45 for 15 minutes, take a 35- to 40-minute lunch near Alexandria around 11:45, and make a final 10- to 15-minute stop around Lafayette at 2:00. With roughly 7 hours 40 minutes of driving plus those stops, the normal arrival is about 3:45 p.m. I would treat 4:30 p.m. as the planning time to absorb construction or heavier I-10 traffic.
Wait, both rooms start check-in at four, correct? I do not want to arrive at 3:45 and have that treated as the plan.

Correct. Standard check-in begins at 4:00 p.m. at both hotels. The schedule should be framed around a 4:00 to 4:30 arrival, not early check-in. Cambria’s stated arrival window runs from 4:00 p.m. to midnight, and Bourbon Orleans lists 4:00 p.m. through 11:59 p.m. Even with a two-hour delay beyond the buffered estimate, you would arrive around 6:30 p.m., comfortably inside either window.
What does the first evening look like from each one? We will not want a major attraction after that drive. Dinner and a little walking are enough.

From Cambria, you can valet once, settle in, walk to dinner in the Warehouse District, and take a short loop along Julia Street or toward the river without committing to the busiest part of the Quarter. From Bourbon Orleans, dinner and a short walk are immediately outside the hotel: Royal Street, Jackson Square, and the riverfront are all convenient, though Bourbon Street noise and crowds are more likely on Saturday night. Neither plan requires moving the car.
Then compare the rest of what we discussed: World War II Museum Sunday, French Quarter Monday morning, and the Garden District Monday afternoon.

Cambria is the cleaner fit for Sunday because the National WWII Museum is roughly a 10- to 15-minute walk. Bourbon Orleans is better for Monday morning because you are already in the French Quarter. For the Garden District, both work with a streetcar or rideshare; Cambria has a modest advantage in avoiding a longer trip back across the Quarter afterward. Across the full itinerary, Bourbon Orleans saves walking mainly on the Quarter portion, while Cambria is better positioned for the museum and still workable for the other stops.
So is the Quarter convenience worth the extra $90.19 and the smaller beds? Give me the choice, not another neutral comparison.

Choose Cambria. It saves $90.19, gives the three of you the more comfortable sleeping arrangement, offers a later cancellation deadline, and fits the museum-heavy Sunday especially well. The Bourbon Orleans location is useful for Monday morning, but that single advantage does not outweigh the added cost and narrower beds when the rest of the itinerary is split between the Warehouse District, French Quarter, and Garden District.
Before I act on that, tell me exactly what still needs one last check. Keep it limited to things that could change the recommendation.

Recheck the Cambria checkout page immediately before booking for December 20-23 with two adults and one 14-year-old: total room charges of $657, lodging tax of $109.72, no mandatory property fee, and the same flexible cancellation terms. Yes. Because the reservation is guaranteed, the room should be held overnight, but the call will prevent the arrival from being treated as a possible no-show. Ask the agent to add a late-arrival note and repeat the revised ETA back to you.

That makes the arrival margin important. Show me the hotel choices before you total everything. I would rather stay at the retreat resort if it fits, but I am open to nearby.

The retreat venue has a standard king at $239 per night. Two nights, lodging tax, and the mandatory resort charge come to $611.62. Its king studio totals $421.36 for two nights, including tax, with breakfast and parking included; cancellation is allowed until 11:59 p.m. local time on May 11.
For the nearby hotel, include transportation back and forth to the meetings. I do not want a total that assumes someone else drives me.

For a PSP trip without a rental, I would allow $96 total for airport rides and $46 for four short rides between Homewood Suites and the venue. For the venue hotel, the PSP airport rides are about $84 total. With the Ontario rental, local meeting transportation is already covered.
Okay. Give me complete totals for the sensible combinations, including every mandatory fee you have identified.

Here are the four practical combinations: PSP nonstop plus the Renaissance is $1,157.62: $462 flight, $611.62 hotel, and $84 airport rides. PSP nonstop plus Homewood Suites is $1,025.36: $462 flight, $421.36 hotel, $96 airport rides, and $46 meeting rides. ONT nonstop plus rental car plus the Renaissance is $1,155.62: $318 flight, $226 rental and fuel, and $611.62 hotel. ONT nonstop plus rental car plus Homewood Suites is $965.36: $318 flight, $226 rental and fuel, and $421.36 hotel. All four remain under the $1,200 ceiling.
That Ontario and Renaissance total is almost identical to Palm Springs and Renaissance. Is there any reason to choose it?

Not on cost. It saves $144 on airfare but gives that back in rental and fuel, and it adds the long drive in both directions. Its advantage is the earlier scheduled arrival: 7:28 a.m. at ONT versus 9:38 a.m. at PSP. Even so, the PSP itinerary has enough scheduled margin and avoids freeway traffic, a rental counter, and the return drive to Ontario.
How dependable is the PSP arrival if the flight is delayed? I cannot walk in after the opening starts.

The scheduled margin is 4 hours 52 minutes before registration. Allowing 15 minutes to leave the aircraft, 10 minutes to reach the pickup area, and 45 minutes for the ride still puts you at the resort around 10:50 a.m. A two-hour flight delay would move that to about 12:50 p.m., leaving roughly 1 hour 40 minutes. A delay approaching three and a half hours would threaten the 2:30 deadline. Among these options, the early PSP nonstop is the cleanest dependable plan because it has substantial buffer without a connection or long ground transfer.
And the Ontario flight? Earlier sounds safer on paper.

On schedule, it reaches ONT seven hours before registration. Using 30 minutes to deplane and collect the rental, 20 minutes at the counter, and two hours for the drive puts arrival near 10:20 a.m. It can absorb a larger flight delay than PSP, but part of that advantage is exposed to rental delays and variable traffic through the Inland Empire. I would still call it dependable, especially with the rental reservation completed in advance, but it involves more failure points.
I am leaning toward PSP and staying at the venue. It is only about $132 more than the cheapest PSP combination, correct?

Correct. The venue combination is $1,157.62, which is $132.26 more than PSP plus Homewood Suites at $1,025.36. In exchange, you eliminate four meeting rides and any concern about being separated from the retreat schedule. You would still have $42.38 of reimbursement room.
Before I decide, does that remaining amount need to cover anything obvious, like a hotel fee you left out or a bag charge?

The $611.62 hotel figure already includes lodging tax and the mandatory resort charge, and the airfare needs no checked-bag allowance because you are taking only a carry-on. The $84 ground figure is an estimate, so surge pricing or gratuity could exceed it. Meals, personal incidentals, and the hotel’s refundable card hold are not included. If your $1,200 cap must also cover gratuities, I would reserve about $15 and treat the usable cushion as roughly $27.
Then make the recommendation, but do not book anything yet.

Choose the DFW-PSP nonstop and stay at the Renaissance Esmeralda. The complete working total is $1,157.62, leaving $42.38 under the cap before optional ride gratuities. Their message says the front desk is staffed all night, but they want notice after 10:00. Can you draft a short reply?

I need to work out Denver for October 8 and 9. I can compare complete combinations. Is the dinner also near the Colorado Convention Center, and does the $800 exclude transportation between your home and the Dallas airport?
Yes, the dinner is at a restaurant about two blocks from the convention center. The allowance excludes my transportation at home, so only count Denver airport transfers and local travel there.

That helps. I found two workable flight patterns to compare. A Dallas Love Field itinerary is $356 round trip: Wednesday 8:40 a.m. to 9:45 a.m., then Thursday 3:10 p.m. to 6:10 p.m. A DFW itinerary is $298 round trip: Wednesday 9:25 a.m. to 10:35 a.m., then Thursday 2:05 p.m. to 5:07 p.m. Both are nonstop and the quoted totals include taxes. So the 2:05 is possible by car but not comfortable by train. What are the hotel choices? I need somewhere I can walk to both events.

No breakfast or other amenities need to be part of the comparison. Give me the rail and car costs from the airport.

The RTD airport fare is currently estimated at $10 each travel day, so budget $20 round trip. From the airport, the A Line goes to Union Station; reaching either hotel then requires a walk of roughly 20 minutes or a short downtown connection. Hired rides are running about $40 to $55 each way before any unusual surge, so $90 round trip is a reasonable planning figure. Your dinner and panel would not require additional transportation from either hotel.
Build the totals both ways. Use Home2 first.

With Home2, the DFW flight and rail total $537.24: $298 airfare, $219.24 hotel, and $20 rail. Substituting hired rides brings that to about $607.24. And Hyatt Place would add $33.64 to each one, correct?
Correct. The Hyatt Place combinations are $570.88 for DFW plus rail, about $640.88 for DFW plus hired rides, $628.88 for Love Field plus rail, and about $698.88 for Love Field plus hired rides.
Compare the schedule margins on Wednesday too. I do not want the dinner to be the only thing I can make if a flight is delayed.

The Love Field flight reaches Denver at 9:45 a.m., leaving 8 hours 45 minutes before dinner. The DFW flight arrives at 10:35 a.m., leaving 7 hours 55 minutes. Even allowing an hour to deplane and travel by rail, both put you downtown around midday. A delay of two or three hours would still leave useful afternoon time before the 6:30 dinner. Love Field provides 50 minutes more protection, but neither Wednesday schedule is fragile.
Thursday matters more. If I take the 3:10 flight, lay out the rail timing after the 10:15 panel.

For a 3:10 p.m. departure, aim to be at DEN around 1:10. If you are out of the panel by 10:30 and have your stored bag by 10:45, you have 2 hours 25 minutes to reach the airport. Allowing about 20 minutes to Union Station, up to 30 minutes waiting for a train, and roughly 40 minutes on the A Line gets you to DEN around 12:15. That leaves about 55 minutes beyond the two-hour airport target. Even one missed train should still be manageable.
That is better. Is there any reason to pay for Hyatt Place over Home2 for this schedule?

Not from the facts that affect this trip. The walking difference is about a minute, both are positioned well for the dinner and panel, and both list complimentary luggage storage. Hyatt Place costs $33.64 more. Home2 is the stronger value unless its live rate has a restrictive cancellation term or Thursday storage cannot be confirmed.
Use Home2 and the Love Field flights, with rail as the planned transportation. I might use a car Thursday only if the panel runs late. What should I budget for that mixed case?

The selected baseline is $595.24. If you use the $10 rail fare Wednesday and a hired ride Thursday estimated at $45, the trip becomes about $630.24. Using the upper end of the Thursday ride estimate, $55, produces $640.24. That still leaves $159.76 under the allowance.

Good. I am not asking you to book yet. Give me the exact option to price again and the checkpoints before I submit it.

Reprice the nonstop Love Field itinerary for October 8 at 8:40 a.m., arriving Denver at 9:45 a.m., and October 9 at 3:10 p.m., arriving back at 6:10 p.m.; the current round-trip total is $356 including taxes. Confirm free Thursday luggage storage through at least 11:00 a.m., check the cancellation deadline, and verify the A Line service schedule for both travel windows. I repriced Denver. I need to settle the flights now because both hotel options have cancellation clocks running. Can we compare the actual schedule risk, not just the fare?

Wednesday is either the 8:40 a.m. nonstop from Love Field, landing at 9:45, or the 2:45 p.m. nonstop, landing at 3:50. Thursday is either 1:35 p.m., landing at Love Field at 4:35, or 3:10 p.m., landing at 6:10. The dinner starts at 6:00 Wednesday. My panel is supposed to finish at 11:45 Thursday.

If the panel ends at 11:45, you could collect stored luggage by about noon and take an A Line departure around 12:15 to 12:30. A hired ride shortly after noon would provide a similar or slightly better margin depending on traffic. It is workable, though you should still leave promptly when the panel ends.
And the 1:35 really is too tight, correct? I would rather hear that plainly.

Correct. To have a reasonable airport margin for 1:35, you would need to leave downtown near 11:30 or earlier. That means leaving the panel before its scheduled end, and even then a delayed departure from downtown would create unnecessary risk. I would not pair that return with this agenda.

The 8:40 outbound with the 3:10 return is $356 total. It is a standard coach fare: changes are allowed without a change fee, but I pay any fare difference; cancellation returns a flight credit, not cash. The cheaper fare is basic and cannot be changed. Is the extra cost justified?

Yes. The $356 combination protects the dinner, lets you attend the full panel, and retains useful change value if the forum schedule moves. Even before assigning a value to the missed dinner or panel time, the savings are too small for the schedule exposure.

Understood. I’ll treat nonstop service as a requirement only for this Denver forum. Among the eligible choices, the 8:40 a.m. Wednesday departure and 3:10 p.m. Thursday return are the clear pair.
Choose that $356 round trip. Before I submit, tell me the airport-transfer plan and the exact final checks. I will decide between the two hotels immediately afterward.

Choose the October 8 nonstop from Dallas Love Field at 8:40 a.m., arriving Denver at 9:45 a.m., and the October 9 nonstop at 3:10 p.m., arriving Love Field at 6:10 p.m., for $356 including taxes. Before payment, confirm both dates, airport codes, nonstop status, total, and that the fare permits changes with only a fare difference and returns a credit upon cancellation. Choose Home2. Give me the payment and transit details I should preserve with the confirmation.

The airline changed my Thursday flight home from Denver. It now leaves almost two hours earlier, so I cannot make it after the panel. Can you look at the rebooking choices without touching Wednesday's flight?

Confirm that only the October 9 return is changing; the October 8 outbound remains intact. Parking is the swing item: approximately $90 at a streetcar-line hotel or $150-$165 in the Warehouse District or near the Quarter. That makes driving transportation roughly $268-$343. That is a bigger gap than I expected. What hotel areas would you consider? I do not want us in a room with one bed and a pullout unless there is no reasonable alternative.

I would compare three zones. The Warehouse District is easiest for Saturday: the CAC is a short walk, and the aquarium is about a 15-minute walk or brief ride. Two-queen rooms are common, but rates and parking are higher. The Canal Street edge of the French Quarter gives you good access to the aquarium and restaurants, while the CAC is about 15-20 minutes on foot; noise varies by block and valet parking is usually expensive. Along St. Charles Avenue in the Garden District, rates and parking can be lower and two-queen rooms are available, but the streetcar is slow enough that I would allow 30-40 minutes to reach either activity on a holiday weekend.
Give me one realistic hotel in each area, with the full three-night number for two queens. We are not looking for luxury.

Using refundable planning rates and including estimated hotel taxes: Hotel Fontenot in the Warehouse District is about $846 for three nights in a room with two queen beds. The Hampton Inn on St. Charles in the Garden District is about $738 with two queens and breakfast; estimated parking is $30 nightly, or $828 with a car. Exact inventory and cancellation deadlines need live verification before purchase.
The Carondelet one sounds like it might be the middle ground. Is it actually convenient to both places, or does the map make it look better than it is?

It is a legitimate middle ground. It is roughly 0.8 mile to the CAC, about an 18-minute walk, and around 0.9 mile to the aquarium. The aquarium route is straightforward toward the river. For Saturday, you could walk to the CAC if the weather is good or take a short ride. The immediate block is busier than the Garden District but not deep in the Bourbon Street nightlife corridor. Its main drawbacks are valet cost if you drive and occasional street noise, so requesting a room away from the street would matter for this stay.
Now put the two sensible combinations side by side. I think those are driving with the St. Charles hotel and flying with either Carondelet or the Warehouse District.

Driving plus the St. Charles hotel is approximately $1,096: $828 for room and parking, $125 fuel, $18 tolls, $35 road food, and about $90 for three days of streetcar fares and occasional rides. Wait, if we drive Friday and arrive after one in the morning, is the hotel definitely going to keep the room? I do not want the reservation treated as a no-show.

A guaranteed reservation should be held, but an arrival after midnight needs direct handling because the property may run its nightly audit before you reach it. The reservation should show arrival on Friday the 16th, not Saturday, and the hotel should be called that afternoon with an estimated arrival around 1:30 a.m. Ask the desk to add a late-arrival note and confirm that the room will not be released. Keep the confirmation number and the name of the employee who acknowledges it.

With one fuel stop, a meal or longer rest break, and normal traffic entering Dallas, plan on 9 to 9.5 hours. Leaving at 2:30 p.m. puts you home around 11:30 p.m. to midnight. A holiday-weekend traffic delay could push that later. By comparison, a nonstop around 4:30 p.m. would require leaving the hotel near 2:00, land at DFW around 6:00, and likely put you home between 7:15 and 7:45 p.m.
That changes it. She has school Tuesday, and midnight is too late. Is there an earlier driving departure that does not waste the whole Monday?

Leaving by 11:00 a.m. is the practical compromise. You could have breakfast, take a short walk, check out, and be home around 8:00-8:30 p.m. Leaving at noon moves arrival closer to 9:30. You would still have Friday night in transit and give up Monday afternoon, but the trip remains about $755 less than flying with Carondelet.

Between the two flying hotels, take Fontenot out. Breakfast and being between the Quarter and the activities are more useful than saving a few rides. Check whether the Saturday morning flight still leaves enough margin if it runs an hour late.

With a one-hour delay, the 7:05 flight would land around 9:32. A conservative curb time of 10:15 and a 30-minute transfer would put you at Carondelet around 10:45. After leaving bags, you could depart the hotel by 11:30 and reach the CAC around noon, leaving about an hour before the 1:00 program. Give me one complete number for each. Include the harbor activity, the arts program, and a reasonable food figure so I can see the family-trip cost.

Show me how the Sunday version lays out. I do not want the Wednesday program squeezed between cross-town plans.

We have the St. Louis spring-break dates settled: Sunday March 16 through Friday March 21, five nights. It will be the three of us. I can compare it door to door rather than looking only at airfare. What flight price and schedule are you seeing, and would you rent a car in St. Louis? For the drive, I will assume you leave from home in Dallas unless there is another starting point.

Home in Dallas. The reasonable nonstop is about $248 each round trip. It leaves DFW at 9:10 Sunday morning and the return leaves St. Louis at 4:35 Friday. We would check one bag. I am not sure about renting a car; that is part of the question.

For three people, airfare starts at $744. Add roughly $70 for one checked bag round trip if the fare does not include it, plus about $108 for six calendar days of DFW parking. A compact rental for five days is likely around $330-$390 after taxes, before hotel parking and fuel. Without a rental, airport rides and trip transportation can be estimated separately.
Now compare that with driving. We can take our own midsize SUV. I do not want an optimistic drive time that ignores stops.

Dallas to St. Louis is roughly 630 miles each way. The map time is around 9 hours, but for three people with fuel, meals, and two or three breaks, I would budget 10 to 10.5 hours each direction. At about 25 mpg, 1,260 highway miles uses roughly 50 gallons. At an estimated $3.05 per gallon, base fuel is about $153; allowing local driving brings fuel to about $175. There are no major toll costs on the straightforward route, though a small contingency is sensible. The real tradeoff is giving up most of Sunday and Friday versus saving several hundred dollars and having the SUV available all week.

Assume we would leave Dallas at 7:00 Sunday morning and could leave St. Louis after breakfast Friday. What does the flight cost with a rental, and what does it cost if we fly and use rideshares instead?

Using planning estimates: fly plus rental is $744 airfare, $70 bag, $108 DFW parking, $360 rental, about $25 rental fuel, and whatever the hotel charges for parking. Before hotel parking, that is about $1,307. Fly plus rideshares is $744 airfare, $70 bag, $108 DFW parking, about $90 total for airport transfers, and approximately $130-$180 for the Forest Park, Fox, and downtown movements. I would carry $1,167 as the midpoint. Driving is about $175 fuel plus hotel and downtown parking, so transportation itself is dramatically cheaper.

Let us work on hotels, because parking could change that. I see the Drury near Forest Park at $1,238 total for five nights with two queens, breakfast, and free parking. There is also a downtown hotel at $196 a night before tax, but it charges $35 a night to park. Would splitting three nights by Forest Park and two downtown make the sightseeing easier?

It would make the downtown day easier, but only one day benefits. A two-night downtown stay adds a hotel move, packing, checkout timing, and about $70 in parking. At roughly 17% tax, the downtown room would be about $459 for two nights before parking, or $529 with parking. If the Drury prorates near $248 per night all-in, three nights there would be about $743, putting the split lodging near $1,272. That is already about $34 above the five-night Drury total, and it does not price the inconvenience of moving.
The Wednesday performance is at 7:30. If we stay by Forest Park all five nights, are we creating a transportation problem for the Fox and downtown?

No. The Fox in Grand Center is only a few miles east of the Forest Park area. With your SUV, allow 15-25 minutes depending on traffic and about $15-$25 for event parking. Downtown is roughly another 10 minutes east; one day of garage parking near the Arch or City Museum should be budgeted at $25-$35. Those two parking charges are much less disruptive and less expensive than changing hotels.
What if we fly and do not rent a car? The Drury says it has a shuttle, but I cannot tell whether that means airport service or just something local.

I would not count on that shuttle until the hotel confirms its route, hours, and whether advance reservations are required. For comparison, assume paid airport transfers. The Forest Park museums can be grouped with walking and short rides, but the hotel-to-attraction distances vary, and March weather may make walking less appealing. The Fox trip and downtown day are manageable by rideshare. Flying without a car works, but it requires more coordination and leaves the local total somewhat variable.

Our daughter would rather have a separate sleeping space than share one room for five nights. I found a one-bedroom suite in Clayton for $1,515 total. Parking is $18 nightly, and breakfast is included. How should that compare with the Drury room?

For five nights, the Clayton suite becomes $1,605 after $90 parking. It gives you meaningful separation and still keeps Forest Park convenient, but it is $367 more than the Drury. Driving with the Drury produces a lodging-and-transport base of about $1,463: $1,238 hotel, $175 fuel, and roughly $50 for Fox and downtown parking. Driving with Clayton is about $1,830. The room configuration is therefore a $367 comfort decision, not a location requirement.
Please include food only where the hotel changes it. Both include breakfast, and I do not want a general meal estimate. Also, does the Drury evening food materially affect the comparison?

I will leave ordinary lunches and dinners out. If the Drury's evening reception is offered on all five dates and is substantial enough for your family, it could replace one or two casual dinners, but I would not assign savings until the current schedule and menu are verified. Treat it as potential upside rather than money needed to make the option fit.

May 12 through May 14. I can land late Wednesday if that makes the trip less rushed. Include all three, but not meals. I will have one carry-on suitcase.

Does the Hilton have somewhere secure to leave my suitcase Tuesday morning? A 10:26 arrival obviously will not get me a room before noon.

From a 10:26 a.m. scheduled landing, the current estimate is 35 to 55 minutes by taxi or rideshare to the hotel, so you would likely reach it between 11:15 and 11:35 a.m. After leaving the bag, you would have roughly two hours before the meeting.
Spell out both schedules using the Hilton and the 2:20 return. I want to know the realistic meeting margins, including airport travel.

Monday-to-Wednesday: depart DFW Monday at 6:35 p.m., arrive BOS at 11:15 p.m., and reach the Hilton around 12:05 a.m. Tuesday. That is the part I do not like. Is there an earlier flight Monday that does not have me checking in after midnight?

There is a 3:10 p.m. nonstop from DFW arriving at 7:52 p.m. It is $497 round trip with the 2:20 p.m. Wednesday return, or $59 more than the 6:35 p.m. Monday option. Estimated hotel arrival is 8:40 to 9:00 p.m., which gives you a normal night's sleep and removes Tuesday flight risk.

Can the hotel hold my bag after checkout, and is that partner office still walkable?

We have June 7 through June 15 available for a San Diego trip, but we only want six nights. It will be the three of us. Can you compare the date combinations before we get attached to a hotel?

How awkward is the move? Lay out which days would go where.

I'm not comfortable leaving luggage in the car at the zoo. Can the move work without that?

Yes. Ask the coastal hotel to hold the bags after checkout, visit the zoo, then return north to collect them before driving downtown. That adds roughly 45 to 60 minutes of driving. Candidate one is the Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central, in a room with two queen beds. The current five-night price is $1,925 before mandatory taxes and fees and $2,248 estimated all-in. It is about a 5- to 12-minute walk to many Theater District venues and roughly 15 minutes on foot to Grand Central. Candidate two is Hyatt Place New York/Chelsea, also quoted with two queen beds. Its five-night total is $1,742 before taxes and mandatory charges, or $2,036 all-in. From there, allow about 20 to 25 minutes by subway or 20 to 35 minutes by car to either activity. Neither quote includes parking, which you do not need here.
Does either include breakfast? And are those totals for all three of us, not per person?

Yes, each hotel total covers one room for all three guests for five nights. The Hyatt Place rate includes breakfast for registered guests. The Hilton Garden Inn rate does not; breakfast is available for purchase. Wi-Fi is included at both. The quoted room categories explicitly list two queen beds, though the final booking page should still be checked before payment because New York inventory changes quickly.
Can you put the four flight-and-hotel combinations side by side with transfers? Leave meals and the two activities out, but include anything else that is mandatory in the quotes.

Using the all-in room prices and the car-transfer allowances: LGA plus Hilton Garden Inn is about $4,045 ($1,647 flights + $150 transfers + $2,248 hotel). LGA plus Hyatt Place Chelsea is about $3,833 ($1,647 + $150 + $2,036). JFK plus Hilton Garden Inn is about $3,857 ($1,389 + $220 + $2,248). JFK plus Hyatt Place Chelsea is about $3,645 ($1,389 + $220 + $2,036). These estimates include the mandatory hotel charges shown and airport transportation, but exclude meals, activities, optional hotel incidentals, and any checked-bag fees.
Interesting. So the central hotel with JFK is only $24 more than Chelsea with LaGuardia.

Correct based on these quotes: $3,857 versus $3,833. That trade is essentially a wash financially. JFK plus the central hotel gives you easier movement during the stay but the longest arrival night. LGA plus Chelsea gives you the cleaner airport schedule, included breakfast, and a longer commute to both fixed activities.
For Saturday, how risky is that late Friday arrival? We do not have anything before the 2:00 matinee, but I do not want one flight delay to wreck the weekend.

Either Friday flight leaves substantial recovery time before 2:00 p.m. Saturday, but the LGA option is the stronger schedule. It departs 45 minutes earlier, lands 54 minutes earlier, and has a shorter transfer. Under normal operations you would reach a Midtown hotel around midnight to 12:30 a.m.; with JFK, approximately 1:00 to 1:30 a.m. A cancellation would be the larger risk with either last-evening pattern, so before ticketing I would check whether the airline has a later same-night flight and what Saturday-morning reaccommodation options exist.
Agreed. I am leaning toward LaGuardia. Is 3:40 Wednesday late enough that we are not wasting the whole day, and early enough that a delay should still get us home before Thursday school?

It is a reasonable balance. You could have breakfast, check out, and keep luggage with the hotel, then leave Midtown around 12:45 to 1:00 p.m. for LGA. The scheduled 6:43 p.m. arrival gives you a meaningful buffer before Thursday morning. It does not eliminate disruption risk, but it is materially better for the school deadline than the JFK flight arriving at 7:49 p.m.

Then narrow it to that LaGuardia schedule and the two hotels. I am not ready to buy today. Before we do, I will need the cancellation terms for both rooms and the flight fare rules, plus a check that the two-queen inventory is really there.

The working shortlist is now the nonstop DFW-LGA itinerary departing Friday, February 13 at 6:45 p.m. and returning Wednesday, February 18 at 3:40 p.m., quoted at $1,647 for three. The lodging finalists are Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central at an estimated $2,248 all-in and Hyatt Place New York/Chelsea at an estimated $2,036 all-in with breakfast. Including a $150 round-trip car allowance, the estimated totals are $4,045 and $3,833 respectively. Nothing has been booked. I am ready to settle the New York flights. Compare the real total for all three of us, including one checked bag each, and account for airport cars and how much of Friday and Wednesday the different schedules consume.

The fares have repriced. The LaGuardia pair is still available: Friday DFW-LGA 6:45-11:04 p.m. and Wednesday LGA-DFW 3:40-6:43 p.m. Base airfare is $1,647 for three. One checked bag per traveler each way adds $240, and estimated private-car transfers total $150, bringing the practical total to $2,037. Friday door-to-door is roughly 5:00 p.m. to 12:15 a.m.; Wednesday you would leave a Midtown hotel around 12:45 p.m.
And the alternatives through JFK and Newark? I do not want a cheaper fare that turns into an ordeal.

The JFK outbound leaves DFW at 7:30 p.m. and arrives at 11:58 p.m. Paired with the Wednesday Newark return at 4:55 p.m., arriving DFW at 8:05 p.m., airfare is $1,518. Bags add $270 because that fare charges $45 each way, and the two airport cars are estimated at $235. Total: $2,023. You would reach the hotel around 1:30 a.m. Friday night and leave it near 1:00 p.m. Wednesday. It saves only $14 versus LaGuardia and adds a much later arrival plus a cross-river trip to Newark.
Was there also a JFK round trip, or did that disappear?

It is still there. The same 7:30 p.m. outbound pairs with a 1:25 p.m. Wednesday JFK departure, landing at DFW at 4:38 p.m. Airfare is $1,476, bags are $270, and cars are about $220, for $1,966 total. The drawback is the return: for a 1:25 p.m. flight, I would plan to leave Midtown by 9:30 a.m. It effectively gives up Wednesday morning.
Give me the ticket rules side by side. Also, is the LaGuardia price still for the cabin we discussed, not basic economy?

Correct. LaGuardia is standard main cabin: nonrefundable, changes allowed without a separate change fee, but any fare increase applies; cancellation before departure produces airline credit for each named passenger. Seats can be selected now. The JFK-Newark combination is also nonrefundable, but the outbound is basic economy: no voluntary changes and only limited cancellation credit after a $99-per-person deduction. The JFK round trip has that same basic-economy restriction in both directions, and seat assignments cost extra or may be deferred.
Then LaGuardia is clearly the workable one. Before you buy it, confirm the complete charge today and tell me what seats are actually open.

The ticket charge today is $1,647 total, including taxes, for all three passengers. Checked bags are not prepaid; assuming all three check one bag each way, $240 would be paid at check-in. Available contiguous seats include rows 21 and 24 outbound and rows 18 and 23 return. Each has a three-seat block open, with window, middle, and aisle together at no added charge.
Book it. Put me in a window seat, and seat my spouse and daughter beside me in the same row both ways.

I have the passenger names and payment method from the trip file. The purchase will charge $1,647 now. I will assign you the window, with your spouse in the middle and your daughter on the aisle, keeping all three together on both flights. Shall I submit it?
Yes, submit it.

The flights are ticketed under confirmation NYC8R4: Friday, February 13, DFW-LGA 6:45-11:04 p.m., and Wednesday, February 18, LGA-DFW 3:40-6:43 p.m. The card on file was charged $1,647. Seats are 21A, 21B, and 21C outbound and 18F, 18E, and 18D return, with your seat at the window both ways. Checked bags remain $40 per bag each way. With six bag charges and the $150 car allowance, the projected flight-and-transfer total is $2,037. The LaGuardia timing now supports a late Friday hotel arrival around midnight and a Wednesday hotel departure around 12:45 p.m.; the two hotel candidates remain unreserved pending their room and cancellation checks.
Go ahead and do the hotel checks now. I need the actual five-night totals, not estimates, and make sure the room will legally hold all three of us.

I’ll verify the exact bed setup and occupancy first, then compare taxes, mandatory charges, cancellation cutoffs, late arrival handling, and the added transit cost from each location before reserving anything.
Also, our flight does not land until 11:04 Friday night. I do not want the room released while we are coming in from LaGuardia.

The Hilton Garden Inn Times Square Central has a room with two queen beds listed for two adults and one 14-year-old. That is higher than the earlier number. What exactly does the mandatory charge cover, and when does that rate become nonrefundable?

The destination charge covers the property’s daily food-and-beverage credit and enhanced internet; it cannot be removed even if you do not use those benefits. The rate can be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. New York time on Tuesday, February 10. After that, the penalty is one night’s room rate plus tax, currently $432.23. A card guarantee is required, but the balance is payable at the hotel.
All right. Now check the Long Island City option just as carefully, especially the sleeping arrangement.

The Hyatt Place Long Island City has a larger room with two queen beds and a sofa bed. The hotel confirmed it for two adults and one 14-year-old, with no added-person fee. How do the locations work in practice? Include what we would spend getting to the Saturday and Tuesday plans, and getting back to LaGuardia Wednesday.

From Times Square, the Saturday activity is walkable and Tuesday’s is one subway ride; estimated family transit for both is $17.40. A Wednesday car to LaGuardia is about $75, so the location-adjusted hotel total is $2,423.54. From Long Island City, both activities require subway trips, estimated at $34.80 total for the family. The Wednesday airport car is about $45, bringing that option to $2,057.37. The late-Friday airport ride is already covered by the existing transfer allowance and does not change this comparison.
So Long Island City is $366.17 less even after the extra subway trips, correct?

Correct. The difference between the two location-adjusted totals is $366.17. Long Island City also gives you the confirmed sofa bed in addition to the two queens, but its cancellation deadline is about a day and nine hours earlier.

Book the Long Island City room. Put all three names on it, note that our daughter is 14, and tell them we expect to arrive around midnight or a little after. I want the confirmation to show that they will hold it for late arrival.

The Hyatt Place Long Island City is reserved for five nights, Friday, February 13 through Wednesday, February 18, under confirmation HPL-629417. Cancellation is free until 3:00 p.m. New York time Monday, February 9; afterward the penalty is $395.51. With estimated activity transit and the Wednesday airport ride, the location-adjusted lodging total is $2,057.37.

I need a round trip from Atlanta to Chicago for an exhibition opening. I have to be at the museum by 1:00 p.m. Tuesday, October 14, and I’ll return Friday, October 17, but the Friday timing is still uncertain.
I can narrow down the outbound now and keep a few return possibilities open. Is this for one traveler, and should I search both O’Hare and Midway?
One traveler. Please check both airports. The museum is downtown, and I need enough time after landing to get there before the crate handoff at 1:00.

Allowing time to deplane, collect any checked equipment, and travel downtown, I would target an arrival no later than about 10:30 a.m. Do you want nonstop flights only, or should I include a connection if it saves substantially?
Nonstop for the outbound. I don’t want a connection putting the handoff at risk. Economy is fine.

There are three workable nonstop outbound windows: an early flight reaching O’Hare around 8:00 a.m., a later departure arriving at O’Hare around 9:35 a.m., and a Midway option arriving close to 10:05 a.m. The first two leave more recovery time; the Midway flight has the tightest margin. Which should I focus on?
Compare the first two. I don’t need to arrive at eight if the 9:35 arrival still gives me a reasonable buffer.

The 9:35 O’Hare arrival should leave roughly two and a half hours before the handoff, though traffic or a baggage delay could reduce that. The earlier option gives about four hours and is currently $74 more. Both are nonstop economy flights.

Keep the 9:35 arrival as the leading outbound, and note the earlier one as backup. Now let’s look at Friday. The opening activities end that evening, but I’m waiting to hear whether I have to stay for a post-opening handoff.
What is the earliest time you might realistically leave the museum if the handoff is brief, and how late would you be willing to depart Chicago?
Best case, I could leave the museum at 4:30 p.m. More likely it will be around 6:00, and if there is a problem I may not get out until 7:30. I’d still rather come home Friday than add a hotel night.

That creates three useful return bands. A flight around 7:15 p.m. from Midway works only in the best case. A nonstop around 9:05 p.m. from O’Hare is more realistic if you finish near 6:00. There is also a late nonstop near 10:20 p.m. from Midway that could work after a 7:30 release, but the transfer would still need to go smoothly.
Drop the 7:15 option; that sounds too fragile. Can you hold the 9:05 O’Hare and 10:20 Midway choices as the short list without booking either one?

Yes. I’ll leave both as unbooked candidates: the 9:05 p.m. O’Hare nonstop for a likely 6:00 p.m. finish, and the 10:20 p.m. Midway nonstop for a later release. Fares and seats can change until one is selected.
Good. Please summarize the outbound choice and those two return options so I can send the timing to the museum team.

Outbound for Tuesday, October 14: leading choice is a nonstop economy flight from Atlanta arriving at O’Hare at about 9:35 a.m., leaving roughly two and a half hours to reach the museum before the 1:00 p.m. crate handoff. Backup is the earlier nonstop arriving around 8:00 a.m., currently $74 more. Friday, October 17 return short list: a 9:05 p.m. nonstop from O’Hare if you leave the museum near 6:00 p.m., or a 10:20 p.m. nonstop from Midway if the post-opening handoff keeps you until roughly 7:30. Nothing has been booked; the return choice remains pending confirmation from the museum.

The museum has confirmed I have to stay through 6:30 Friday evening. Please compare the full round-trip choices now, including one checked case for installation tools. I need to know which return is actually workable.

Understood. I’ll compare the two Tuesday outbound flights with the Friday returns, then include the checked-case charge in each total. Before I calculate it, is the tool case under 50 pounds and within standard checked-bag dimensions? Also, does it contain any batteries, compressed gas, solvents, or other restricted materials?
It is a normal hard-sided case, about 42 pounds. No gas or solvents. There is one cordless drill, but I carry the removable battery in my hand luggage.

That should price as one standard checked bag. Keeping the loose lithium battery in your carry-on is also the correct handling, subject to the airline’s terminal inspection. I found three sensible combinations. The leading Tuesday outbound still leaves Atlanta at 8:15 a.m. and reaches O’Hare at 9:35 a.m. The earlier backup leaves at 6:40 a.m. and arrives at 7:58 a.m. Both are nonstop economy flights.
And what does Friday look like now that 6:30 is fixed?

The 9:05 p.m. O’Hare departure is technically possible, but I would not treat it as dependable. From the downtown museum, you would have only 2 hours 35 minutes before departure. Friday traffic, unloading the case, checking it, and security could consume most of that window. The flight is nonstop and arrives in Atlanta just after midnight.
Agreed. I do not want the museum handoff rushed just to chase that flight. What about the 10:20 from Midway?

That one is materially safer. It departs Midway at 10:20 p.m. and arrives in Atlanta at 1:15 a.m. Saturday. Leaving the museum around 6:40 p.m. would generally put you at Midway roughly between 7:10 and 7:35, depending on traffic, leaving close to three hours or more for the bag drop and security. It is also nonstop.
Good. Now give me the actual totals, not just the base fares.

With standard economy rather than basic economy, the combinations price as follows at the moment: the 8:15 a.m. outbound paired with the 9:05 p.m. O’Hare return is $286 airfare plus $70 for the checked case round trip, totaling $356. The same outbound paired with the 10:20 p.m. Midway return is $332 plus $70, totaling $402. The 6:40 a.m. backup outbound paired with the Midway return is $406 plus $70, totaling $476.
Is the $70 definitely for both directions? I do not want another case fee appearing at the airport.

Yes. It is $35 each way for one standard case up to 50 pounds, so $70 for the trip. The quoted totals include that charge in both directions. They do not include an overweight fee, which should not apply at the stated 42 pounds, or optional seat upgrades.
Are these all on one ticket even though I would arrive at O’Hare and leave from Midway?

The $402 option is issued as one multi-city itinerary: Atlanta to O’Hare on Tuesday and Midway to Atlanta on Friday. The airport change does not require any transfer during travel because it occurs across your Chicago stay. The checked case is paid separately for each flight segment but included in the $402 trip total I gave you.
Does using Midway create any issue with returning a rental car?

Only if you plan to rent one at O’Hare and return it at Midway; that could add a one-way location fee. No rental car is currently part of this itinerary. If you are using local transportation between the airport, hotel, and museum, the different airports do not create an additional booking obligation.
No rental car. The museum is arranging transportation from O’Hare on Tuesday, and I can take a car to Midway Friday. Compare the two Midway combinations directly.

Both use the same 10:20 p.m. nonstop return and include the same $70 checked-case cost. The difference is Tuesday morning: the 8:15 a.m. departure arrives at 9:35 a.m. and totals $402, while the 6:40 a.m. departure arrives at 7:58 a.m. and totals $476. The earlier flight buys another 1 hour 37 minutes in Chicago for $74 more. Either leaves enough time to reach the museum before the 1:00 p.m. crate handoff, assuming the arranged pickup proceeds as planned.
Then the earlier one is not worth the extra $74. Select the 8:15 outbound and the 10:20 Midway return at $402 with the case included.

Selected itinerary: Tuesday, October 14, nonstop Atlanta to O’Hare departing at 8:15 a.m. and arriving at 9:35 a.m.; Friday, October 17, nonstop Midway to Atlanta departing at 10:20 p.m. and arriving at 1:15 a.m. Saturday. Standard economy airfare is $332, and one standard checked case at $35 each way brings the current total to $402.
Before I approve purchase, confirm that standard economy allows advance seat selection and that changing the return would not mean forfeiting the whole ticket.

Confirmed. This standard economy fare allows advance selection from available regular seats. It is not a basic-economy ticket. Changes are permitted under the displayed fare rules without a separate change penalty, though you would owe any fare difference if the replacement flight costs more. Changing the return segment would not automatically forfeit the outbound after it has been flown. The itinerary is selected but not yet purchased, and the $402 total remains subject to availability until ticketing.

The museum added Saturday morning inventory checks, so use Tuesday, October 14 through Saturday, October 18. My return is now Saturday afternoon. I need something under the approved $240 nightly room cap, and the 7:00 a.m. Wednesday installation call makes the commute important.
I’ll compare rooms available for all four nights and separate the nightly room rate from taxes or mandatory fees. What museum entrance should I use for the commute estimate?
Use the staff entrance on South Michigan Avenue, near the loading area. Walking would be ideal that early, but a simple direct transit ride is acceptable.

Three available options fit the room-rate cap. The Silversmith Hotel has a standard queen at $229 per night, about an 8-minute walk from the staff entrance; the four-night total is $1,087 including taxes. Staypineapple on West Washington has a queen room at $214 per night, about a 13-minute walk, totaling $1,016. Club Quarters Central Loop has a standard room at $189 per night, about 17 minutes on foot or roughly 10 minutes using one direct bus, totaling $899. None of these rates shows a mandatory destination fee.
Is the Silversmith rate flexible? I don’t want the whole stay locked in while the Saturday flight is still only selected.

Yes. The $229 rate can be canceled without charge until 6:00 p.m. local time on October 12. After that, the penalty is one night plus tax. There is also a prepaid rate at $207, but it is nonrefundable and would not suit the unresolved flight.
Agreed. My wife will join me Thursday evening and stay through checkout Saturday, but we’ll use the same room. Does that change the price?

No. The flexible rate allows two adults at the same $229 nightly room rate, so adding her does not increase the lodging total. The available room choices at that rate are one queen bed or one king bed; no separate-bed setup is required unless you want one.
Choose the queen room. That’s what I prefer when the two of us are sharing one room, and there’s no reason to pay for a different category here.

The standard queen remains available for all four nights at $1,087 total. Before I reserve it, note that the room is compact, at approximately 260 square feet. The king category is $18 more per night, while the cancellation deadline and included Wi-Fi are the same.
The queen is fine. The short walk matters more, especially Wednesday morning. Is there any issue reaching the staff entrance by 6:50 a.m.?

No scheduled transit is needed. The walking route is about half a mile along well-traveled downtown streets and is estimated at 8 to 10 minutes at that hour. Leaving the hotel at 6:35 a.m. gives a modest buffer for the staff entrance and security check.
Reserve that flexible queen room for October 14 through October 18. Put both occupants on the reservation, but keep the work billing under my name.

The flexible standard queen at the Silversmith Hotel is reserved for four nights, checking in Tuesday, October 14 and checking out Saturday, October 18. Avery Thompson is the primary guest and billing contact, with your wife listed as the second occupant. The confirmed total is $1,087 including taxes, with no mandatory hotel fee shown. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. Chicago time on October 12; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. The hotel is approximately an 8- to 10-minute walk from the museum’s South Michigan Avenue staff entrance.

The airline just moved my Friday return to 5:40 p.m. That will not work with the museum handoff at 6:30. Can you find something later Friday, or Saturday morning if Friday is impossible? Please leave the outbound alone.

The Tuesday outbound is unchanged. For the return, there is a nonstop from Midway at 10:20 p.m. Friday that arrives in Atlanta at 1:15 a.m. Saturday. The airline can move you to it for $26 more. There is also an 8:10 a.m. Saturday nonstop from O’Hare, arriving at 11:05 a.m., with no additional fare.
How much time would the Midway flight leave after the handoff? I do not know whether it will take thirty minutes or an hour.

If the handoff runs until 7:30 p.m., you would still have about two hours and fifty minutes before departure. Allowing roughly 35 minutes by car to Midway at that hour would put you there around 8:05, a little over two hours before the flight. Traffic could lengthen that trip, but the timing is workable.
That is better than adding Saturday travel. Is the 10:20 flight still available in standard economy, and can the airline apply the schedule-change waiver?

Yes. Standard economy is still available, and because the airline changed your original departure, the waiver removes the $26 fare difference. Your advance seat selection remains available, though the exact seat from the original flight cannot carry over automatically.
Go ahead and confirm the Friday 10:20 from Midway. Do not change anything else.

The return has been changed to the nonstop departing Midway at 10:20 p.m. Friday, October 17 and arriving in Atlanta at 1:15 a.m. Saturday. There was no additional charge under the schedule-change waiver. The Tuesday outbound remains unchanged.
Does this affect the Silversmith reservation, or do I need another night because the arrival is after midnight?

No extension is needed. The Silversmith reservation already runs through checkout on Saturday, October 18, so you can keep the room through Friday evening and leave for Midway after the handoff. The hotel dates, occupants, billing contact, and cancellation terms remain unchanged.

I need to start planning a weekend in Raleigh for my aunt's retirement dinner. It is Saturday, November 15 at 6:00 p.m. My wife and I would leave Atlanta after work on Friday. We originally thought we would return Monday, but she may need to be back Sunday night instead.

I can compare both trip lengths without committing you to either return date. I’ll look at round trips for two adults from Atlanta to Raleigh-Durham, departing Friday, November 14 after work, with return options on Sunday, November 16 and Monday, November 17. I’ll also compare a shared hotel room for two versus three nights. Are there any fixed Friday obligations that determine how early you can leave?
We can get to the Atlanta airport by about 5:15 p.m. Nothing else is fixed. Please show a neutral range first. We have not decided on airline, nonstop versus connection, seats, or the room setup.

The first useful Friday comparison includes these currently displayed choices for two adults: Delta nonstop departing Atlanta at 6:35 p.m. and arriving Raleigh-Durham at 8:00 p.m., with round-trip totals starting at $468 for a Sunday return or $512 for a Monday return; Southwest nonstop at 7:25 p.m., arriving 8:50 p.m., starting at $486 Sunday or $498 Monday; American connecting through Charlotte at 6:10 p.m., arriving 9:42 p.m., starting at $421 Sunday or $447 Monday; and United connecting through Washington Dulles at 5:55 p.m., arriving 10:06 p.m., starting at $438 Sunday or $459 Monday. Those are standard search results before choosing fare type, seats, or return flight. The 5:55 and 6:10 departures could be tight if you only reach the airport at 5:15.
Agreed. Keep them visible for comparison, but I would not count on making either early one. What do the return choices look like on Sunday and Monday?

For Sunday, the broad range includes Delta nonstops at 4:45 p.m. and 8:15 p.m.; Southwest nonstops at 5:30 p.m. and 9:05 p.m.; an American itinerary through Charlotte at 6:20 p.m.; and a United itinerary through Dulles at 3:55 p.m. Monday has Delta nonstops at 9:10 a.m., 1:40 p.m., and 6:25 p.m.; Southwest nonstops at 10:35 a.m. and 4:50 p.m.; American connections at 8:15 a.m. and 2:25 p.m.; and a United connection at 11:05 a.m. The listed round-trip totals vary with the outbound pairing, so I have not treated any one combination as selected.

The Sunday evening possibilities would let us have most of that day with family. Monday could be useful too, but only if my wife is cleared to take the day. Can any of these fares be held while we wait?

None of the lowest displayed fares has a free multi-day hold. Delta and United currently offer a 24-hour risk-free cancellation window after purchase when booked directly and far enough before departure. American shows a complimentary 24-hour hold on eligible itineraries, but only until the displayed deadline tomorrow; alternatively, direct purchase generally has the applicable 24-hour cancellation protection. Southwest shows cancellation back to the original form of payment on its refundable fare, while the lower fare has different credit rules. A hold or cancellation window would buy roughly one day, not enough if her answer will take several days.
She expects to know by Wednesday, so a one-day hold does not solve it. Is there a sensible way to protect the hotel without deciding between Sunday and Monday yet?

Yes. The cleanest temporary structure is a cancellable three-night reservation from Friday through Monday, provided the cancellation deadline falls after Wednesday. Once her schedule is confirmed, you could shorten it to a Sunday checkout, subject to the hotel retaining availability and the same nightly rate. Another option is separate reservations for Friday-Sunday and Sunday-Monday, but that can create a room-change risk and different cancellation deadlines.
Show me a few hotels that work for the family dinner. It is near the North Carolina Museum of Art, but do not narrow by bed type yet.

For one shared room and two adults, three relevant refundable options are showing. The StateView Hotel is about a 10- to 12-minute drive from the museum, at $219 per night plus tax, with cancellation until 6:00 p.m. on Wednesday, November 12. The Hyatt Place Raleigh/Cary is roughly a 12- to 16-minute drive, at $176 per night plus tax, cancellable until 11:59 p.m. Wednesday. The Holiday Inn Raleigh Downtown is around a 10- to 15-minute drive depending on traffic, at $158 per night plus tax, cancellable until 6:00 p.m. Thursday. Each has multiple room configurations in the current results, and I have left those unselected.
Can you give me the actual totals for two nights and three nights? I want to see the cost of keeping Sunday night open.

The displayed totals including estimated taxes are: StateView, $496 for Friday-Sunday or $744 for Friday-Monday, a $248 difference; Hyatt Place Raleigh/Cary, $402 for two nights or $603 for three, a $201 difference; Holiday Inn Raleigh Downtown, $361 for two nights or $541 for three, a $180 difference. Parking, incidentals, and any optional charges are not included unless collected in the quoted room rate.
Could we reserve three nights now and simply cancel the last night on Wednesday, or would that require canceling the whole reservation and starting over?

The policies shown allow changes before the cancellation deadline, but they do not guarantee that shortening the stay preserves the original nightly rate. In practice, the hotel may reprice the remaining two nights when the checkout date changes. The reservation would not necessarily have to be canceled in full, but I would treat the quoted two-night amount as a current comparison rather than a guaranteed future adjustment.
Then check whether splitting off Sunday night would cost much more at those three. I do not want to create a complicated arrangement for a difference of a few dollars.

We are free from Saturday, September 20 through Sunday, September 28. Compare the total for two adults. We would share one hotel room. In either area we would want a car for beach access, meals, and day trips.

That gives you two straightforward seven-night spans: Saturday September 20 to Saturday September 27, or Sunday September 21 to Sunday September 28. Yes. Also account for the fact that we would need to get from Atlanta airport back home after returning the rental. We can use about $45 each way for that. We would leave our own car at home if we fly.

Understood. For Tybee/Savannah, the drive is about 250 miles each way and generally 4 to 4.5 hours without a long stop. For St. Simons or Jekyll, it is roughly 310 to 325 miles each way and about 5 to 5.5 hours. I’ll compare those with flights from Atlanta to Savannah and Brunswick, including a rental car and the $90 home-airport transfer total.
Please do. We are not trying to avoid driving at all costs. I mainly want to know whether flying actually saves enough time to justify the added expense.

For September 20-27, current sample totals for two are approximately: drive to Tybee/Savannah, $245 including fuel, estimated wear allowance, and hotel parking; fly to Savannah and rent a car, $1,040 including two round trips, rental, taxes, fuel, airport transfers, and hotel parking. Door to door, flying saves only about 1 to 1.5 hours each way after airport time. For St. Simons/Jekyll, driving is about $315. Flying to Brunswick with a rental is near $1,180 and has limited schedules; flying to Savannah and driving south is about $1,025 but takes nearly as long door to door as driving from Atlanta.
That makes driving look fairly clear. Are the Sunday-to-Sunday figures materially different?

The driving totals change very little. For September 21-28, Tybee/Savannah remains about $245, while St. Simons/Jekyll is about $315. The sample airfare is lower on the Sunday departure: Savannah flights plus the rental total about $910 for Tybee and about $925 if you continue to the Golden Isles. Brunswick is still the costliest option at roughly $1,110. Even with the lower fares, flying adds about $600 to $865 over driving.
How much vacation time do we lose by driving to each? We could leave Atlanta around 8:30 in the morning on either start date.

Leaving at 8:30 a.m., you would likely reach Savannah around 1:00 p.m. and Tybee around 1:30, allowing for one stop. St. Simons would be around 2:00 p.m., and Jekyll around 2:15. Those arrivals line up reasonably well with afternoon hotel check-in. A flight might put you on Tybee around noon if every step goes smoothly, but the Brunswick-area options would generally place you there between 1:00 and 3:00 p.m. because of schedules and rental pickup.

Then remove flying to Brunswick. Keep the Savannah flight only as a benchmark, not as the likely choice. Now compare the two date spans from a destination standpoint. I am concerned about weekend crowds and hotel prices.

September 20-27 places your first night on Saturday but has a Saturday checkout. September 21-28 avoids paying for the opening Saturday night, though it includes the following Saturday night and a Sunday return. Preliminary one-room lodging samples show the Sunday-to-Sunday span about $110 lower around St. Simons/Jekyll and about $70 lower around Tybee/Savannah. Tybee’s weekends show the sharper rate increase and more two-night restrictions. The Golden Isles sample is steadier across both spans.
What about the practical difference between the areas? We want beach time, but seven nights is long enough that we need more than sitting on the sand.

Tybee/Savannah offers the broader non-beach mix: Savannah’s historic district, museums, architecture, restaurants, and riverfront are about 25 to 40 minutes from Tybee depending on traffic. The tradeoff is heavier weekend traffic, paid parking, and a busier beach setting. St. Simons/Jekyll offers quieter coastal days, bike routes, maritime and historic sites, nature centers, and easy movement between the islands. Brunswick adds dining and a small historic core, but the overall sightseeing range is narrower than Savannah’s.

A split stay could preserve both experiences, but changing hotels during a seven-night trip adds packing and check-in time. Do not split the stay yet. Which combinations are strongest if we care about overall value, useful things to do, and not spending a large part of the first and last day in transit?

The strongest overall-value combination is St. Simons/Jekyll, Sunday September 21 to Sunday September 28, driving from Atlanta. It has the lowest sampled lodging week for that area, predictable transportation costs, and arrival near check-in time. The strongest activity-rich combination is Tybee/Savannah on the same Sunday-to-Sunday dates, also driving.
